name: Snapchat
tagline: Camera-first messenger where snaps, stories and streaks disappear · the app is the friend graph

pricing.notes: Base app is free; Snapchat+ is the optional tier (39.99 USD/yr annual, pricier Platinum tier removes most ads). Official page shows the price in-app, not on the web.

verdictSummary: The mechanics one-shot fine: ephemeral photo messages, 24-hour stories and streak counters are CRUD plus a delete timer. None of that is the product. Snapchat is where your friends already are · the value of a disappearing photo is who is on the other end, and a self-hosted clone with two users is a group chat with extra steps. Add the AR lens stack built on years of face-tracking models, screenshot detection that needs OS-level app privileges, and media infrastructure moving billions of snaps a day, and the honest verdict is that the network is the app. The prompt below is the consolation build: a private snap relay for one friend group that opts in.
coreLoopDIY: Snap a photo with a caption overlay and send it to an invited friend group; each snap deletes after one timed view, with daily streaks and 24-hour group stories.
requirements: a small VPS or free-tier Node host with HTTPS (camera and push APIs require it)
friends willing to install the PWA and actually use it
whatYouLose: the people: everyone you snap with is on Snapchat, not on your server
AR lenses and filters backed by years of face-tracking models
screenshot detection · a web app cannot see or stop screenshots
Snap Map, Discover, Spotlight and the creator ecosystem
reliable mobile push · web push on iOS is best-effort, not messenger-grade
moatNotes: the graph is the product; lenses are frontier computer-vision models; snaps ride a global media pipeline
whyPeopleStillPay: Almost nobody pays for Snapchat itself · the app is free and the subscription sells cosmetics and vanity telemetry: pin a #1 BFF, see who rewatched your story, wear a badge. People pay 3.99 USD because the network underneath is where their friends live, and status inside a graph only matters in a graph with people in it. That is also exactly why a rebuild is pointless: you can clone every feature and you will have cloned none of the value.

prompt:
Build a private ephemeral photo-messaging app (snaps for one friend group) in an empty folder.
Stack: Node 22 with Fastify and better-sqlite3, and a vanilla-JS PWA served from /public with no build step; do not offer alternative stacks.
Core loop: open the camera with getUserMedia, capture a photo, type or draw a caption overlay on a canvas, and send it to one or more friends.
A snap is viewable exactly once for up to 10 seconds; the server deletes the image file immediately after the view and keeps only a minimal sent/opened log row.
Accounts are invite-code only: the admin seeds codes with a CLI script; signup is username plus passcode, and sessions are httpOnly cookies.
Track per-pair daily streaks server-side and show the count next to each friend.
Add group stories: a snap posted to my story is visible to all members and hard-deleted after 24 hours by a sweep job.
Store media as files on disk outside the web root; store metadata in SQLite with WAL mode.
Add web push notifications for new snaps behind a permission prompt; the app must work fully without them.
Make the PWA installable with a manifest and service worker, and an offline shell that caches the UI but never caches snaps.
HTTPS is required for camera and push: document local dev with a self-signed cert and production behind Caddy.
Secrets (VAPID keys, session secret) go in .env; ship .env.example and a documented script that generates the keys.
Be honest in the UI: label view-once as deleted from our server, and state plainly that screenshots cannot be detected on the web.
Include empty, loading, expired-snap and failed-upload states.
Write tests for the delete-after-view flow, the 24-hour story sweep, and streak day-boundary math using a fake clock.
Write a README covering setup, deploying on a cheap VPS, where data lives, how deletion actually works, and how to invite friends.
Deliberately out of scope: AR lenses and face filters, Snap Map, Discover or Spotlight feeds, video calls, and any screenshot detection.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, external storage, or third-party auth.
Finish by running the tests and printing the exact commands to start the server and create the first two users.
